subject: Hospitality
title: Virtual Reality Travel
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Virtual Reality Travel.

hook.text: Can VR replace travel? Some hotels now offer virtual tours so immersive that guests 'visit' before they book.

buildup.text: Marriott's VRoom service let guests experience destinations in VR from their hotel room. The concept tested well.

discovery.text: VR travel appeals to those who can't travel—elderly, disabled, or budget-limited people who still crave experiences.

twist.text: Studies show VR actually increases desire to travel in person. It's a marketing tool, not a replacement.

climax.text: Hotels will use VR for previews and upsells. 'Tour the presidential suite in VR' could become a booking conversion tool.

punchline.text: VR won't kill travel. It sells it. A preview makes the real thing irresistible.

quiz.question: How does VR travel affect people's desire to travel in person?
options: It actually increases the desire to travel in person
